Oliver — great to hear and thanks for the clear questions. I sketched a workable structure below (high level) and attached a term-sheet draft with a worked example. Key points:

- Wallet + burn model: we create a prepaid wallet representing the committed $ value. Usage is drawn from the wallet. Unused funds are treated according to the expiry/ramp option chosen (see options A/B).
- Ramped drawdown (recommended): year 1 ramp: 30% Q1 / 25% Q2 / 25% Q3 / 20% Q4 (by committed $) to align with your expected cadence. Years 2–3 default to an even monthly amortization unless we agree a new ramp.
- Fallback credit shelf: we can provision a smaller, recurring "fallback credit" pool (10% of annual commit) priced at a reduced discount level — this covers burst needs without moving to on-demand pricing. Any usage that exceeds the wallet + fallback is billed at on-demand rates.
- True-up cadence: quarterly true-ups with 60-day post-quarter reconciliation. Excess unused wallet funds can either: 1) credit next period (option A, 12-month carry), or 2) be returned as a one-time credit to be applied to the following year (option B, expiry at contract anniversary).

Discounting and tiers (illustrative):
- $1M+/yr: 18% off hosted list
- $3M+/yr: 25% off hosted list
- Quantization/feature credits: additional technical credits/discounts for larger reserved GPU commitments (discussed separately)

I attached a short term-sheet draft (RWI-9821-term-sheet-draft-v1.pdf) that shows an example 2-year commitment with the ramp above and an 10% fallback credit shelf. Can you confirm which expiry option (A or B) Procurement prefers, and whether quarterly true-ups are acceptable?

If this looks broadly OK, I can circulate internally for finance and legal to prepare a redline. Happy to jump on a quick call early next week to walk the numbers.

Naomi / Marcus — quick notes from finance:

1) Revenue recognition & amortization
- If wallet is prepaid and refundable only at anniversary, we recognize revenue ratably over the committed period. A heavy Q1 draw doesn't materially change recognition, but it does front-load cash.

2) Ramp sensitivity
- Q1-heavy vs Q3-heavy: short-term impact on cash flow timing. Recommend adding a minimum monthly consumption floor equal to 5% of annual committed $ to mitigate churn/earn-out risk.

3) Fallback credit accounting
- Treat fallback credits as a separate liability bucket; price them at a smaller discount (we recommend list - 8pt). Unused fallback credits should be treated similar to a promotional liability and recognized according to chosen expiry policy. Option A (12-month carry) is easier operationally; Option B (anniversary expiry) is cleaner for P&L but less flexible for the customer.

4) Early termination / true-up
- Recommend quarterly true-ups with a 60-day settlement window. For early termination, propose pro rata refund of unused wallet after offsetting any committed minimums and an early termination fee equal to 3% of remaining committed value (negotiable).

I've attached a simple finance model that shows the cash & revenue effects under three ramp scenarios.

Oliver / team — thanks for the clear framing. A few commercial suggestions from me (ops/legal lens):

- Alternative drawdown: consider a rolling consumption bucket where credit expires 18 months after purchase rather than strict 12-month carry or same-year expiry. This gives you operational flexibility while protecting Redwood from long-tail exposure.
- Canary ramp: we can include a staged ramp with a mid-year review checkpoint. If usage is below the 60% of expected mid-year target, we trigger an optional amendment window to re-price or re-route to dedicated capacity (safety valve).
- Fallback credit shelf: operationally we prefer a capped monthly redemption rate from the shelf to avoid large negative impacts in a single month. E.g., cap at 25% of monthly committed draw.

Attached is a redlined term sheet with the operational language I think we should push. If legal is OK, I can send this to BlueVine as our preferred redline. Also recommend using DocuSign for the final execution.
